title: B2B ABM Go-Live: Activation Membership Without SFMC Duplication

moves.dialogueText: "ABM is in two weeks. Buying committees mean one Contact on several Accounts. Mapping a real Account Contact relationship adds a day of harmonization we do not have—can we just project Contact onto Account Contact and keep moving?"

options.text: Spend the modeling day: Account Contact as the account–person relationship (e.g. AccountContactRelation), related to Account and Individual/Contact.
options.techDebtImpact: Burns schedule on DMO harmonization, but leaves a Customer 360 relationship grain that activation can membership on later.

options.text: Map Account Contact 1:1 from Contact so modeling finishes today and activation planning can start tomorrow.
options.techDebtImpact: Saves ~1 day now, but collapses many-to-many Account–person roles. Later membership work cannot express “this Contact in this Account” without duplication.

moves.dialogueText: "The junction DMO is still category Other. Flipping it to Profile means recreate-or-transform work and re-testing relationships—half a sprint—before it shows under Activation Membership. Ship Other and hope the UI lists related DMOs?"

options.text: Leave category Other and protect the sprint; Activation Membership should accept any DMO related to Account or Contact.
options.techDebtImpact: Keeps the calendar intact, but Other-category junctions never appear under Activation Membership—marketing will fall back to Contact grain.

options.text: Pay the recreate/transform cost: set the junction to Profile, re-relate Account and Contact, then expose it under Activation Membership.
options.techDebtImpact: Consumes schedule on category change and remap, but Profile is what Activation Membership filtering expects for relationship-grain export.

moves.dialogueText: "Dry run: one Contact on two Accounts → two Contact rows in the Shared DE. Re-segmenting on the junction and rewiring membership is another build day. Leadership says activate on Contact and let SFMC dedupe—do we take that shortcut?"

options.text: Keep membership on Contact/Individual and lean on SFMC subscriber keys / journey dedupe so we do not rebuild the activation.
options.techDebtImpact: Avoids a rebuild day, but person-grain membership multiplies Shared DE rows per related Account; journeys inherit the duplication.

options.text: Rebuild: segment on Profile junction rows, set Activation Membership to the junction, traverse attributes to Contact/Individual as needed.
options.techDebtImpact: Costs a rebuild cycle, but membership matches the B2B relationship grain so Account sharing stops exploding Contact rows.

moves.dialogueText: "Compliance wants every Contact Point Email in the DE. Max # of Attribute Values is stuck at 1. A fan-out transform plus new segment/activation is another multi-day track—can we just raise the attribute limit instead?"

options.text: Schedule the transform track: fan-out DLO/DMO (one row per Individual–email), segment on it, activate with membership on that grain.
options.techDebtImpact: Burns multi-day scope on transform + re-activation, but payload can choose a contact identifier per email row for compliance.

options.text: Raise Max # of Attribute Values on Contact Point Email (or a file-based activation DMO) and keep the existing membership object.
options.techDebtImpact: Looks like a same-day config win, but native activation will not fan out multiple emails per Individual via that limit—secondary addresses never become addressable rows.

moves.dialogueText: "Activation fails because three attributes named Id collide across Individual, Contact Point Email, and the Redshift DMO. I can give them preferred activation names this afternoon, or we rebuild the Redshift DMO with non-overlapping field names first—three days, past go-live. Which do we do?"

options.text: Assign preferred activation names to the three colliding Id attributes and re-run the activation today.
options.techDebtImpact: Saves three days now at no later cost: the collision lives in the activation payload, so distinct names fix the Data Extension columns without touching the model.

options.text: Rebuild the Redshift DMO with non-overlapping field names, then re-run the activation after go-live.
options.techDebtImpact: Buys a tidier source model, but spends three days past go-live on a collision that payload names already resolve.
